Local Goods: brand directions

Options only. Step 2 of the October 23 plan. Nothing in the app has changed. Pick one direction and one logo; step 3 applies it.

These directions are original designs. Local Goods is not affiliated with the Golden Triangle BID or WMATA. All merchants and people shown are fictional demo data.

Theme:

Golden Triangle

“Spend inside the triangle.”

Names the rule in four words: the credits work here, in this district.

Owning the district's own shape makes Local Goods feel native to downtown DC, and navy with gold reads like a serious payments product. Biggest risk: it ties the brand to one district's name and must never be mistaken for the BID's own branding, and navy-and-gold can drift toward a generic private bank.

Transit lines

“Reroute your lunch.”

The commute-desk-commute loop, with one stop added in the neighborhood.

Showing merchants as stops on the route you already take tells the whole story in one picture: the same daily loop, rerouted through the neighborhood. Biggest risk: map language invites comparison with Metro, so the colors and line style must stay clearly our own, and the line motif can get busy on small screens.

Storefront

“Spend local. Prove it.”

Keep the current line: the awning carries “local”, and the precise UI underneath carries “prove it” (ledger, receipts, fraud check).

Awnings and sign-painted lettering put the corner café first, while the clean, precise UI underneath makes it trustworthy enough to handle money. Biggest risk: warm-and-crafty is the most common look for buy-local projects, so without discipline it reads as a farmers' market flyer instead of a payments product.
